newsitem.title: USA: Greater world wheat total seen focus of USDA data.
newsitem.headline: Greater world wheat total seen focus of USDA data.

text.p: A "topside" increase of two million tonnes for 1996-97 world wheat production could be revealed Thursday by the U.S. Agriculture Department in its December Supply/Demand (S/D) reports, analysts said.
"A total two million additional production but that would be topside and the carryover will not be increased drastically," said Dean Witter Reynolds grains analyst Jerry Gidel.
The government's December crop report will be released at 0730 CST/1330 GMT Thursday.

Estimates on the report will encompass world and U.S. supply/demand revisions but will not include an updated forecast for 1996 U.S. crop production. Those numbers will be released in USDA's final crop report for 1996 production slated for release at 0730 CST/1330 GMT on January 13.
In its November report, USDA forecast the world wheat crop for the 1996-97 crop year at 579.06 million tonnes and wheat carryout at 110.79 million tonnes.
Gidel and others are expecting USDA Thursday to show an increase in its wheat production outlook for Canada, Australia and Argentina.
"There will be a slight increase in Canada's crop and the Australian crop and Argentina may be up to 15.5 million, a one-million-tonne increase," Gidel said.
Gidel said the trade is expecting Argentina's final crop to be 16.0 million to 17.0 million tonnes, although those figures are unlikely to be indicated on Thursday's report.
In November, USDA pegged Canada's wheat crop at 29.8 million tonnes, Australia's at 21.0 million and Argentina's crop at 14.5 million tonnes.

Since USDA will not change its estimate for U.S. corn or soybean production on this report, traders and analysts will be eyeing a possible shift by the government in its estimate for U.S. export sales.

"The market is hoping soybean exports will be increased but I don't think that's going to occur," said Chicago-based John Kleist, Director of Agriculture Research for ING Futures and Options, a commodity brokerage firm with international affiliations.
"Buyers are covered now and can wait for the South American crop," he said.

In November, USDA pegged 1996-97 U.S. soybean exports at 870 million bushels, above the previous outlook for 850 million bushels. U.S. soybean ending stocks were estimated in November at 210 million bushels, above the previous outlook for 195 million.
In November, world ending stocks for soybeans were pegged by USDA at 17.99 million tonnes, above the outlook in October for 17.78 million.
There are ideas USDA eventually will trim its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. corn exports but the adjustment probably will not surface in the December report, analysts said.
"I'm looking for a decrease in corn exports but this is a December report and USDA probably will leave it alone. They won't make a change until the January report," Kleist said.
In November, USDA said 1996-97 U.S. corn exports would total 1.95 million bushels and ending stocks would tally 1.107 billion bushels.
The world's corn carryout was pegged by USDA in November at 79.28 million tonnes, above the October forecast for 73.37 million.
